dva-ini-049.text: As a recurrent practice of safety hygiene, what the AWS recommends to do periodically with user key accesses IAM which need to exist?
options: Share them among team members to reduce the amount of keys
Post them on the internal wiki to facilitate access
Rotate them regularly: create the new key, update the applications, disable and then delete the old one
Print and save on paper as a single copy
dva-ini-049.explanation: Periodic rotation limits the window of use of a eventually leaked key; the flow with intermediate deactivation allows to reverse without downtime if something still uses the old one.
dva-ini-049.hint: Static key that needs to exist must at least have a term of validity in practice: rotate, migrate, retire.
optionRationales: Periodic rotation limits the window of use of a eventually leaked key; the flow with intermediate deactivation allows to reverse without downtime if something still uses the old one.
Sharing credentials destroys individual traceability and expands exposure.
Wiki is a repository of broad knowledge — disclosing credentials there is direct exposure.
Inviable operationally and without any gain — correct control is rotation and minimal use of static keys.

dva-ini-050.text: A developer of the A account needs to temporarily access resources in the B account of the same company. The security team set up a role in the B account relying on the A account. What service/operation the developer uses to obtain temporary credentials for this role?
options: Request key accesses from account manager B
AWS STS with the AssumeRole operation, which returns temporary credentials of the B account roll
Create an additional root user in the B account
Close account B within account A
dva-ini-050.explanation: Security Token Service issues short-term credentials: AssumeRole on the trusted role of the B account grants temporary and auditable access, without creating permanent users or keys in the other account.
dva-ini-050.hint: The 'temporary token counter' of AWS: Take the roll and receive credentials with time to expire.
optionRationales: Security Token Service issues short-term credentials: AssumeRole on the trusted role of the B account grants temporary and auditable access, without creating permanent users or keys in the other account.
Transferring permanent credentials between people is basic violation — the correct mechanism are roles and STS.
Each account has a single root — and you never use root for routine access.
There is no cloning of accounts — access between accounts is resolved by trust between roles.

dva-ini-051.text: A Bucket S3 of an application keeps internal customer documents. The team wants a lock in the configuration that prevents that QUALQUER political or ACL make this content public, even by mistake from a developer. Which resource applies this protection?
options: Move objects to the Standard-IA class
Enable bucket versioning
S3 Block Public Access enabled in the pocket (or account))
Rename the bucket with a hard to guess name
dva-ini-051.explanation: Block Public Access overlaps with policies and ACLs: with it active, public concessions are blocked or ignored — the network of protection against accidental exposures.
dva-ini-051.hint: The master's gift S3 that vetoes public access even when someone tries to grant.
optionRationales: Block Public Access overlaps with policies and ACLs: with it active, public concessions are blocked or ignored — the network of protection against accidental exposures.
Version protects against loss of versions — not against public exposure.
Storage class treats cost/access — irrelevant for public visibility.
Darkness is not access control — listings and leaks reveal names.

dva-ini-052.text: One API no API Gateway will be consumed by partners, and the team wants to distribute a key to each partner in order to apply Throttling and monthly quotes per consumer. API Gateway implements this control, and what security relief applies?
options: API keys, which are the official user authentication mechanism of the API Gateway
Separate internships for each partner
Distribute credentials IAM account for each partner
API keys associated with use plans — remembering that API keys control consumption and identification, but do not replace authentication/authorization
dva-ini-052.explanation: Use plans with API keys apply throttling and quotes per consumer; as keys are not strong authentication mechanism, real security should come from autors (Cognito/IAM/Lambda).
dva-ini-052.hint: Key API measures and limits the consumption of each partner — but the real 'identity crack' is another mechanism.
optionRationales: Use plans with API keys apply throttling and quotes per consumer; as keys are not strong authentication mechanism, real security should come from autors (Cognito/IAM/Lambda).
API keys identify consumers for measurement/limits — documentation is explicit in not using them as authentication.
Delivering account credentials to third parties is extremely serious — partners receive key API and/or appropriate federation.
Internships separate publishing environments — do not apply consumer quotes.

dva-ini-053.text: For a bucket S3 may invoke a function Lambda when new objects are created, the service must be authorised S3 Calling the function.?
options: No. Security Group function
In the execution role of the function
In the bucket tags
In the resource-based policy of the function Lambda, allowing the main s3.amazonaws.com invokes it from that bucket
dva-ini-053.explanation: The function-based policy (lambda add-permission) authorizes other services/accounts to invoke it — this is how the S3 wins the right to shoot the function in the events of the bucket.
dva-ini-053.hint: To 'who can call me', the function has its own glued policy NELA (resource), not in the role.
optionRationales: The function-based policy (lambda add-permission) authorizes other services/accounts to invoke it — this is how the S3 wins the right to shoot the function in the events of the bucket.
Execution roll defines what the OPERATION can do in services — not who can invoke it.
Security Groups network traffic in VPC — do not authorize invocations between services.
Tags are organizational metadata — do not grant permissions.

dva-ini-054.text: In an IC/CD pipeline with AWS CodeBuild, the build needs a token of access to a private package registry. What is the recommended way to provide this secret to the buildspec without exposing it in the repository?
options: Print token in build logs for reuse
Reference the secret in the buildspec from the Secrets Manager or Parameter Store (SecureString), with the service role of CodeBuild authorized to read it
Send token by message to the team to each build
Save token to buildspec.yml commit
dva-ini-054.explanation: The buildspec supports variables coming from secrets-manager and parameter-store: the value is injected in build time, outside the source code, with access controlled by the project roll.
dva-ini-054.hint: The buildspec knows how to search for values 'in the safe' at build time — the repository never sees the secret.
optionRationales: The buildspec supports variables coming from secrets-manager and parameter-store: the value is injected in build time, outside the source code, with access controlled by the project roll.
The buildspec lives in the repository — secret there is secret leaked.
Logs are widely accessible and retained — never to contain secrets.
Manual secret distribution is insecure and unautomated.

dva-ini-055.text: A company requires multifactor authentication for all users IAM Humans who access the console, as additional protection against stolen passwords. MFA adds to the login process?
options: A second password stored by the user
Manual approval of the administrator at each login
A second possession factor (authenticator application code or physical key) required beyond the password
Automatic encryption of all user's pocketes
dva-ini-055.explanation: The MFA combines 'something you know' (sign) with 'something you have' (device) — an empty password is no longer enough for the invader to enter.
dva-ini-055.hint: Password (what you know) + device (what you have) = two factors.
optionRationales: The MFA combines 'something you know' (sign) with 'something you have' (device) — an empty password is no longer enough for the invader to enter.
Two passwords remain the same (knowledge) factor — the MFA requires a different nature factor.
MFA is authentication control — does not configure storage encryption.
The MFA is automatic with the user's own device — does not involve human approval of third parties.

dva-ini-056.text: A developer noticed that tables of the DynamoDB recently created displays enabled cryptography, although no one has configured it. What is the correct explanation?
options: It is a console display error; the data is in clear text
The DynamoDB encrypts all tables at rest by default, using keys managed by AWS, with switching option for customer keys
Another developer manually activated and hid the configuration
Encryption only exists in tables with secondary indexes
dva-ini-056.explanation: Cryptography at rest is native and compulsory in DynamoDB: by default uses property keys of the AWS, and the customer can choose keys KMS managed by AWS or by himself.
dva-ini-056.hint: Some services were born with the factory locked safe — the DynamoDB He's one of them..
optionRationales: Cryptography at rest is native and compulsory in DynamoDB: by default uses property keys of the AWS, and the customer can choose keys KMS managed by AWS or by himself.
No need to activate — the service applies rest encryption to all tables since creation.
The indication is real — there is no table DynamoDB no cryptography at rest.
The protection covers all tables, indices and streams — regardless of GSIs.

dva-ini-057.text: An application in EC2 access a bank RDS PostgreSQL. In secure network configuration, as a rule of Security Group of the RDS follow good practice to allow only this application?
options: Entry into all doors for the VPC whole
Door entrance 5432 having as its origin Security Group of the implementing bodies
Door entrance 5432 open for 0.0.0.0/0
No entry rules, connecting via exit door
dva-ini-057.explanation: Restricting the door of the bank to the origin of the application SG ensures that only members of that group reach the RDS — dynamic (follows the Auto Scaling) and minimum.
dva-ini-057.hint: Exact port + origin 'app group crack' = minimal and dynamic access.
optionRationales: Restricting the door of the bank to the origin of the application SG ensures that only members of that group reach the RDS — dynamic (follows the Auto Scaling) and minimum.
Bank exposed to the entire internet is one of the most exploited errors — violates the least network privilege.
All ports for the whole network far exceeds what is needed — only the PostgreSQL port, only for the application.
Without entry rule in the bank's SG, application connections are blocked — exit rules of call do not replace entry authorization.

dva-ini-058.text: In the assessment of permissions of the IAM, a request does not correspond to any statement Allow in the applicable policies. What is the result and what concept explains this behavior?
options: The request is pending by 24 hours
The IAM ask the administrator in real time
The request is allowed, because there was no explicit prohibition
The request is denied: the IAM denies by default (implicit deny) anything that is not explicitly allowed
dva-ini-058.explanation: The model of IAM part of the implicit deny: without an applicable Allow the action is denied, and an explicit Deny wins any Allow — the basis of the 'closing by default'.
dva-ini-058.hint: No. IAM, silence means 'no': everything starts denied until someone allows.
optionRationales: The model of IAM part of the implicit deny: without an applicable Allow the action is denied, and an explicit Deny wins any Allow — the basis of the 'closing by default'.
It is the opposite: the absence of permission already denies — the IAM does not work as 'freed except prohibition'.
The evaluation is automatic and instantaneous — no interactive approval.
There is no queue — the verdict is immediate: denied without Allow applicable.

dva-ini-059.text: The logs of an application recorded the complete body of the requests, including card and password numbers — discovered during an audit.?
options: Compact logs to make reading difficult
Never record sensitive data: mask or remove secrets, passwords and card data before logging in
Disable all application logs
Log everything, because the logs of CloudWatch are secrets by nature
dva-ini-059.explanation: Logs replicate for analysis systems, backups and large teams — sensitive data on them have seen permanent leak; sanitization at origin is mandatory (and required by standards such as PCI DSS).
dva-ini-059.hint: What falls into the log spreads — sensitive data masks ANTES to write.
optionRationales: Logs replicate for analysis systems, backups and large teams — sensitive data on them have seen permanent leak; sanitization at origin is mandatory (and required by standards such as PCI DSS).
Logs have wide audience and retention — they are not safes, and access to them is usually less restricted than production data.
Without logs there is no diagnosis or audit — the solution is to sanitize, not blind the operation.
Compaction is reversible and is not security control.

dva-ini-060.text: One SPA (single-page application) hosted in a domain calls a API no API Gateway in another domain, and the browser blocks responses with cross-source policy errors. What configuration solves the problem on the side of the API?
options: Disable the HTTPS of API
Increase integration timeout
Enable CORS the API, returning the Access-Control-Allow-Origin (and related) headers appropriate for the domain of the SPA
Ask users to use another browser
dva-ini-060.explanation: The CORS is the mechanism that authorizes distinct origins in the browser: a API needs to respond to the prelights OPTIONS and include the permission headers for the application domain.
dva-ini-060.hint: Different domains in the browser require that the API 'authorize origin' in the headers — the acronym is four letters.
optionRationales: The CORS is the mechanism that authorizes distinct origins in the browser: a API needs to respond to the prelights OPTIONS and include the permission headers for the application domain.
The blockage is of policy of origin, not of TLS — remove HTTPS only degrades safety.
All modern browsers apply to same-origin policy — the correction is on the server, not the client.
Timeout has nothing to do with cross-source blockage.
